original_value: This study explores neovascularisation and lesion detection in an integrated framework for gradation in diabetic retinopathy (DR). Imaging is assumed to be done from sub‐sample measurements following compressed sensing. Blind estimation of the scale of the matched filter (MF) followed by fuzzy entropy maximisation is done for extraction and classification of the thick and the thin vessels. Mutual information (MI) between vessel density and tortuosity of the thin vessel class is maximised in two dimensions (2D) for neovascularisation detection. For lesion detection, MI between the maximum MF response and the maximum Laplacian of Gaussian filter response is jointly maximised in 2D. The outcomes are then combined in a common platform for gradation in DR. Simulation results demonstrate that 95% images of each of DRIVE, STARE and DIARETDB1 databases and 94% images of MESSIDOR database are correctly graded by the proposed method when 80% measurement space is considered.

result.paraphrase: This study presents an integrated framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading that combines neovascularisation and lesion detection. It assumes imaging from sub-sample measurements under compressed sensing. Thick and thin vessels are extracted and classified using blind estimation of the matched filter (MF) scale followed by fuzzy entropy maximisation. Neovascularisation detection is achieved by maximising in two dimensions (2D) the mutual information (MI) between vessel density and tortuosity of the thin vessel class. For lesion detection, the MI between the maximum MF response and the maximum Laplacian of Gaussian filter response is jointly maximised in 2D. These results are then merged on a common platform for DR gradation. Simulation results show that, with 80% measurement space considered, the proposed method correctly grades 95% of images in each of the DRIVE, STARE, and DIARETDB1 databases and 94% of images in the MESSIDOR database.
